title: Caesar's little secret
prompt:
The line in the stdin box was encrypted the way Julius Caesar liked it: every lowercase letter shifted three places forward, wrapping around the end of the alphabet. The starter reads the line into `secret`; decode it in place and print the result.

Walk the bytes with `ldrb`. For each lowercase letter, shift back by three; if that falls below `'a'`, add 26 to wrap around. Store the decoded byte back with `strb` and leave every other byte alone: spaces, digits, punctuation, and the newline `fgets` kept. The printf at the bottom prints the decoded line.

## what is checked

- the decoded message is printed
- the program exits cleanly
- the decode happens byte by byte in memory (`ldrb` and `strb`, no pasting the answer in)
- the same holds for other lines you do not see: letters that wrap past `'a'`, an empty line, and lines with digits and punctuation
starter:
// decode a message caesar-shifted three letters forward
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(ptr_r, x19)
define(ch_r, w20)

define(LINE_MAX, 256)

        .data
fmt_out:    .string "%s"

        .bss
secret:     .skip 256                       // LINE_MAX bytes

        .text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =secret                 // read the coded line, newline and all
        mov     w1, LINE_MAX
        ldr     x9, =stdin
        ldr     x2, [x9]
        bl      fgets

        ldr     ptr_r, =secret

        // TODO: walk the string byte by byte. Shift every lowercase
        // letter back by three, wrapping so that 'a' goes around to
        // 'x' (add 26 whenever the shift falls below 'a'). Store each
        // decoded byte back where it came from with strb, and leave
        // every other byte and the terminator alone.

        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        ldr     x1, =secret                 // now decoded in place
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
